title: First flight of the Space Shuttle (STS-1)
summary: On 12 April 1981 the orbiter Columbia, flown by John Young and Robert Crippen, lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on STS-1, the first flight of the reusable Space Shuttle. It returned on 14 April. The mission was the first full test of the assembled shuttle system and revealed many problems needing repair.

uncertainty.note: Launch 12 April and return 14 April 1981; the span covers the two-day flight.

beats.caption: Columbia lifted off from Kennedy Space Center at 7 a.m. Eastern with John Young and Robert Crippen aboard.
The orbiter returned to Earth on 14 April, ending a flight of about two days.
As the first full test of the assembled shuttle, the flight exposed roughly 70 problems, so Columbia needed many repairs before its next mission.
